title: Jar drawing sheet
subject: Science

source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 26 (Jar drawing sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 26: Soil in a jar: the shake test. To understand that the different particles in soil settle in layers in water

questions.q: Order these from bottom to top: sand, stones, clay.
questions.model: Ask: which is biggest and heaviest? Stones. They sink first, so they are at the bottom. Sand next. Clay is tiniest, so it is on top.

questions.q: Why is the water still cloudy after one hour?
questions.a: Tiny clay particles are still settling

questions.q: Where would you find the humus?
Set up your shake test with an adult. Draw the jar now. Tomorrow, draw it again and label the layers.
questions.a: Two drawings; second shows labelled layers: stones, sand, silt and clay, water, floating humus
questions.model: Teacher shakes a jar on camera and draws the 'before' picture: one cloudy brown mixture.

questions.q: Which layer is thickest in your jar? What does that tell you about your soil?
questions.a: For example: a thick sand layer means sandy soil

questions.q: Why do rivers leave mud and sand where they slow down?
questions.a: Slow water cannot carry the particles, so they settle as sediment.

questions.q: Big question: what would you see in the jar in the morning?
questions.a: Layers: stones at the bottom, sand, then silt and clay, clearer water, humus floating.
